header:
Problem 3 Solid Electrolyte Interphase
The solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is an important research area in modern electrochemistry. During the first charging of a lithium-ion battery, the electrode potential lies below the reduction potential of the electrolyte, so additives and lithium salts in the electrolyte undergo electrochemical reductive decomposition at the solid-liquid interface. Insoluble solid products deposit on the electrode surface and form a passivation film that is electronically insulating but ionically conducting, thereby slowing electrode corrosion. Vinylene carbonate (VC), a classic film-forming additive, reacts preferentially and promotes formation of a high-quality SEI.

header_images.description: The structures in the figure have the following SMILES: VC, 'O=C1OC=CO1'; EC, 'O=C2OCCO2'.

subquestions.text_open: 3.3 Studies show that VC preferentially undergoes cleavage of a C-O single bond and is reduced to radical anion A carrying 1 unit of negative charge. It then undergoes radical polymerization to form several polymeric products. 3.3.1 In one pathway, A acts as a chain initiator and reacts with VC to form acyclic polymer B. Write the SMILES of B.
rubric: Rubric structure for B: the corresponding SMILES is '*C=COC(=O)O*', where * denotes a repeat-unit connection site. (2 points)

subquestions.text_open: 3.3.4 In the electrolyte, VC can also be electrochemically reduced to lithium oxalate and an enolate. Write the electrochemical reaction equation; EC participates in the reaction.
rubric: Complete reaction: 'O=C1OC=CO1' + 'O=C1OCCO1' + 4$Li^+$ + 4$e^-$ = $Li_2C_2O_4$ + 2$CH_2CHOLi$ (2 points; 1 point if all reactants are correct but the equation is not balanced).
